package_info.package_versions: All versions susceptible if not protected
package_info.why_malicious: The package contains source code that leverages Unicode bi-directional (Bidi) control characters to visually obfuscate the true logic of the code, allowing attackers to hide malicious behavior in plain sight. This results in code that appears benign to human reviewers but executes malicious actions, undermining code review and supply chain security.

execution_context.file_location: Any source file (e.g., main.py, index.js, etc.)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code uses Unicode Bidi control characters to visually reorder conditional logic, causing grantAccess() to be executed for guest users instead of admins, resulting in unauthorized privilege escalation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The presence of Unicode Bidi control characters in source code is highly anomalous and is a known technique for visually obfuscating the true logic of code, enabling attackers to hide malicious intent from human reviewers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal source code should not contain invisible Unicode control characters that alter the logical flow of execution. The actual behavior (granting access to guests) is concealed from reviewers, violating the expectation that code is visually representative of its execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Bidi characters are legitimate in internationalized text content, such as user-facing strings in right-to-left languages, but are never appropriate in code logic, control flow, or comments that affect execution.
key_indicators: Presence of Unicode Bidi control characters (e.g., U+202E, U+202A, U+202B, U+202C, U+2066, U+2067, U+2068, U+2069) within code logic or comments
Mismatch between the visual structure of code and its actual execution logic
Comments or code blocks that appear to close or invert logic unexpectedly
Invisible characters that, when removed, change the meaning or flow of the code

attack_chain.action: Attacker injects Unicode Bidi control characters into source code to visually reorder code tokens and invert logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious logic is hidden from code reviewers, as the code appears benign.

attack_chain.action: Code is reviewed and appears safe due to visual obfuscation, so the malicious code is merged and deployed.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in production environments.

attack_chain.action: At import-time or runtime, the actual logic executes as intended by the attacker (e.g., privilege escalation, unauthorized access).
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of application security or data due to logic inversion or privilege escalation.

behavioral_signatures: Presence of Unicode Bidi control characters in source code files, especially within logic or comments
Mismatch between the displayed code logic and the actual execution logic when Bidi characters are removed
Unexpected privilege escalation or logic inversion at runtime that cannot be explained by the visible code
file_indicators: Source files containing Unicode Bidi control characters (U+202E, U+202A, U+202B, U+202C, U+2066, U+2067, U+2068, U+2069)
Comments or code lines that appear to close code blocks or invert logic unexpectedly
Files where the removal of invisible Unicode characters changes the meaning or flow of the code
network_indicators: Not directly network-related, but may be combined with exfiltration logic hidden via Bidi characters in other attacks
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan all source code files for the presence of Unicode Bidi control characters. Flag any files containing these characters for manual review, especially if they appear within code logic or comments. Use automated tools to compare the logical execution order of code with its visual representation, highlighting discrepancies. Integrate Unicode character detection into CI/CD pipelines to block code containing suspicious Bidi characters before deployment. Review code diffs for invisible character insertions.
